title: Tenant SLA reconciliation and automated crediting playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes the end-to-end process for reconciling tenant SLAs against observed service behavior and issuing automated (or semi-automated) service credits when contractual SLOs are not met. It is intended for Customer Success, Support, Billing, and SRE teams working with enterprise customers on Dedicated and Private deployments. The document covers detection triggers, verification steps, credit calculation, communication templates, ownership, audit trails, and QBR reporting hooks.

Goals and scope:
- Ensure consistent, auditable reconciliation between observed SLA breaches and customer-facing credit outcomes.
- Reduce manual effort for routine reconciliations while retaining human review for complex cases.
- Provide clear timelines and owners for each stage of the reconciliation lifecycle.
- Integrate reconciliation outcomes into QBRs and renewal conversations.

Applicability:
- Applies to enterprise customers with explicit SLA language in contract attachments (latency SLOs, availability SLOs, throughput guarantees).
- Covers both Hosted/Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where Redwood has monitoring/telemetry access or agreed telemetry exports.

Key definitions (SLO/SLA brief):
- Availability SLO: percentage of successful 2xx responses for production tenant routes measured per calendar month (default baseline: 99.9% for Dedicated customers unless contract differs).
- P95 latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency as measured by Redwood telemetry for the tenant's production route(s).
- Incident window: contiguous time range where an SLI drops below the configured threshold for more than the configured degradation-duration (default: 5 minutes).

Detection and alerting (automatic triggers):
1) Telemetry-based alerts (SRE):
   - Alert when tenant-monthly availability falls below SLA threshold OR when P95 exceeds threshold for more than 3 consecutive sampling periods (5m).
   - Alert names/IDs: tenant.slo.availability.breach, tenant.slo.latency.breach.
   - Alert payload must include tenant_id, tenant_org_name, observed_metric, threshold, time_window, and primary SRE runbook link.
2) Customer reports (CS/Support):
   - Support ticket containing reproducible examples, timestamps, and expected vs observed behavior escalates to SLA triage.

Triage and verification workflow (24–72 hour window):
1. Initial Triage (within 4 hours of alert): owner: oncall-sre / support-rotating-operator
   - Confirm alert validity (noise filter): correlate with platform-wide incidents, config changes, and known deploy windows.
   - If global or third-party provider outage: tag as "external" and route to Incident Coordination.
2. Data Collection (within 24 hours): owner: SRE metrics engineer
   - Pull raw request logs, ingress/egress times, model variant IDs, region, pod/node ids, and KV cache hit rates for the incident window.
   - Export telemetry snapshot to archive (S3 path: s3://redwood-slo-audits/{tenant_id}/{year}/{month}/{incident_id}/).
   - Record any service fallback events (model fallback, regional fallback, queued requests).
3. Attribution analysis (24–48 hours): owner: SRE + CS
   - Determine attribution: platform-controlled degradation vs tenant misconfiguration vs customer-origin traffic anomaly.
   - Use checklist:
     - Are there recent tenant config changes? (yes/no)
     - Do request traces show consistent 5xx from Redwood stack? (yes/no)
     - Is KV cache miss spike correlated with latency? (yes/no)
   - Outcome tags: platform, customer, third_party, inconclusive.
4. Resolution and remediation note (48–72 hours): owner: SRE + CS + Support
   - Document remediation steps taken, time windows, and ETA for permanent fix if applicable.

Credit calculation rules and examples:
- Contractual baseline: most contracts define a credit band tied to percent-of-month downtime or latency breach severity. This playbook provides a formula for automated preliminary calculation (subject to legal review if >$X).
- Automated credit formula (preliminary):
  credit_amount = min(max_credit_cap, monthly_commit_amount * breach_fraction * severity_multiplier)
  where breach_fraction = impacted_time_seconds / seconds_in_month
  severity_multiplier (examples):
    - minor: 0.25 (P95 > threshold by < 25%)
    - moderate: 0.5 (P95 > threshold by 25–100%)
    - severe: 1.0 (availability drop > 1% or sustained P95 > 3x threshold)
  max_credit_cap defaults to 50% of monthly commit for automated paths (contracts may override).

- Example 1: Tenant A monthly commit $10,000, 3 hours (10,800 seconds) of availability impact in a 30-day month (2,592,000 seconds): breach_fraction = 0.00417; severity_multiplier = 0.5; preliminary_credit = 10000 * 0.00417 * 0.5 = $20.8 -> round to $21 and flag for review.

Manual review thresholds (escalation to Finance/Legal):
- Any preliminary credit > $5,000 -> manual approval required from Billing Manager and Legal (auto path aborts).
- Attribution tag = third_party or inconclusive -> require SRE and Legal signoff before issuing credit.
- If remediation is partial or customer opted for alternative remediation (e.g., free private support), crediting may be adjusted per contract terms.

Automation pattern (systems involved):
- Triggering system: SLO-alerts -> Ticketing (Zendesk/Jira) -> Reconciliation service (internal microservice: sla-reconciler) -> Billing system (Stripe/Financial ERP)
- Reconciliation service responsibilities:
  - Fetch telemetry archive for incident window
  - Run credit formula with configured contract parameters
  - Generate reconciliation record with audit fields (computed_by, computed_at, telemetry_snapshot_uri, preliminary_amount, attribution_tag)
  - Create Jira ticket with reconciliation details and attach telemetry archive link
  - Post Slack notification to #cs-sla-reconciliations for manual review if thresholds crossed

Audit record schema (stored as JSON blob in Reconciliation DB) - required fields:
| field | description | example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| tenant_id | Redwood tenant UUID | t-123e4567 |
| incident_id | auto-generated ID | inc-20260810-001 |
| computed_by | service/user id | sla-reconciler-v1 |
| computed_at | ISO timestamp | 2026-08-10T14:12:00Z |
| telemetry_snapshot_uri | s3 path | s3://redwood-slo-audits/t-123e4567/2026/08/inc-20260810-001/ |
| preliminary_amount | USD cents | 2100 |
| attribution_tag | platform/customer/third_party/inconclusive | platform |
| approval_status | auto_pending/manual_approved/rejected | auto_pending |

Approval & issuing credits (process):
1. Auto-path (preliminary_amount <= $5,000 and attribution_tag == platform):
   - sla-reconciler auto-creates a billing credit draft and notifies Billing team via Slack and Jira. A 48-hour human review window is opened. If no objection is raised, the credit is applied automatically at 48 hours.
2. Manual-path (preliminary_amount > $5,000 OR attribution_tag != platform):
   - Reconciliation ticket assigned to Billing Manager. Billing Manager reviews audit artifacts and either approves or escalates to Legal. Billing issues customer-facing credit memo and records reason in the tenant ledger.

Communication templates (to customers):
- Initial acknowledgement (sent when SLO incident confirmed and under review):
```
Subject: Redwood — SLA review initiated for {tenant_org_name}
Hi {customer_contact},
We’ve detected a potential SLA deviation for your environment between {start_time} and {end_time}. Our team is collecting telemetry and will provide a recommended remediation and credit estimate within 72 hours. We’ll share the audit artifacts and next steps in the follow-up.
Regards,
Customer Success — Redwood
```
- Credit confirmation (after approval):
```
Subject: Redwood — SLA credit issued for {tenant_org_name}
Hi {customer_contact},
Following our review of the incident on {start_date}, Redwood has issued a service credit of ${credit_amount} in accordance with section {contract_section} of your agreement. Attached: audit-report-{incident_id}.zip
If you prefer an alternate remediation, please reply and we’ll coordinate.
Best,
Billing Operations — Redwood
```

Ownership matrix and SLAs for reconciliation process:
| Step | Primary owner | SLA | Secondary owner |
|------|---------------|-----|-----------------|
| Detection alert | SRE | 5m from breach detection | Support |
| Initial triage | Oncall-SRE / Support | 4 hours | CS |
| Data collection | SRE metrics engineer | 24 hours | Support |
| Attribution analysis | SRE + CS | 48 hours | Legal (if needed) |
| Preliminary credit computed | sla-reconciler | 1 hour after analysis | Billing |
| Final credit applied | Billing | 48 hours after approval | Finance |

QBR integration and metrics for Customer Success:
- Each reconciled SLA incident is recorded as part of the monthly QBR package. The following fields are surfaced in QBR dashboards: incident_count, total_credits_issued, percent_monthly_revenue_credited, mean_time_to_reconcile, attribution_breakdown.
- Talk track recommendation for CS during renewal conversations: present incident context, remediation roadmap, credit outcome, and improvements (e.g., routing changes, KV cache tuning, batching adjustments).

Operational playbook for common scenarios (quick reference):
- Platform-wide outage affecting many tenants: flag as P0, suspend automatic credit application until Incident Command posts final timeline (manual coordination required).
- Tenant misconfiguration discovered (e.g., mistaken rate-limiter policy): confirm customer impact window; crediting allowed only if contract permits. Tag attribution=customer; escalate to CS for remediation and customer advisory.
- Inconclusive telemetry (e.g., private deployment with limited telemetry exports): open forensic request to customer, pause auto-credit path, route to Legal for contract interpretation.

Monitoring and telemetry requirements (minimum):
- Per-tenant SLIs for availability (1m resolution) and P95 latency (5m resolution).
- Request trace id propagation across ingress -> runtime -> model runtime -> response.
- Daily snapshots of tenant traffic distribution and model variant percentages.

Operational checklist for first 90 days of enterprise onboarding (tie-in):
1. Confirm contract SLA fields are encoded in contract parameters in the reconciliation service.
2. Confirm telemetry export for tenant is configured and archived to S3 with retention 13 months.
3. Configure Slack and Jira routing for automatic reconciliations.
4. Run a dry-run (no credit) simulation during the onboarding acceptance window to validate end-to-end audit trail.

Appendices:
A. Example alert rule (Prometheus alert expression):
```
- alert: TenantAvailabilityBreach
  expr: sum(rate(tenant_request_success_count{tenant_id="${tenant_id}"}[5m])) / sum(rate(tenant_request_total_count{tenant_id="${tenant_id}"}[5m])) < 0.999
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Tenant ${tenant_id} availability below SLA"
```
B. Sample reconciliation Jira workflow states: draft -> under_review -> approved -> applied -> closed
C. Contacts and escalation list: CS Lead (Aisha Patel, cs-lead@redwood.com), Billing Manager (Diego Morales, billing@redwood.com), SRE Oncall roster (see internal roster page).
